newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares down, banks and properties lead.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares down, banks and properties lead.

text.p: Singapore shares were lower at midday on Thursday with banks and property stocks leading losers.

"Suddenly there is all sorts of negative news and that has affected sentiment. The fall in Wall Street overnight, the weak regional currencies and the fighting in Cambodia," said a trader with a Singapore firm.
"There is probably not much relation to the Singapore market but we had a decent run up in blue chips a few days ago, so it is time to take a breather," he said.
Singapore Press foreign led losers shedding recent gains and was down 70 cents to Singapore $28.80.
DBS foreign was also down 50 cents to S$19 and City Developments down 40 cents to S$13.30.
Singapore Telecom topped the actives with 4.4 milllion lots changing hands. It fell to S$2.58, down 12 cents.
The Straits Times Industrial index slumped 16.07 points to 1,966.90. Total market volume was 70.46 million shares with 256 losers beating 53 gainers.
Dealers said market sentiment was also weak due to the slump in Malaysian shares traded over-the-counter.
The UOB-OTC index sank to a new year low of 1,107.26, down 10.51 points mirroring the weak Malaysian market.
"Historically, the two markets have very close links. So there is a spill over effect," said one broker.
Malaysia' Renong touched a new year low of S$1.76, down seven cents with 2.78 million shares traded.
